summary: Adds a new published CLI/library package @cipherstash/stack-forge (stash-forge install/push) plus an additive EncryptionClient.getEncryptConfig() accessor in @cipherstash/stack. The material risk is in what the CLI does to customer databases. `stash-forge push` deactivates every eql_v2_configuration row and then inserts the new config as two separate autocommitted statements with no transaction; the config it inserts is the client's own schema, whose cast_as values ('number', 'bigint', 'json') are not in the vocabulary the EQL check constraint accepts (bundled EQL 2.1.8), so for those schemas the INSERT fails after the UPDATE has committed, leaving the database with no active EQL configuration. The same UPDATE also silently discards pending/encrypting configurations. `install` executes whatever SQL is at GitHub 'releases/latest' with no version pin or integrity check. The library change to @cipherstash/stack is additive and low risk. Tests for the new package are mocked unit tests of config loading and the installer only; push and the drizzle path are untested, and no test results were seen.

behaviour_changes.description: New `stash-forge push` writes the client's encrypt config to public.eql_v2_configuration: UPDATE all rows to state 'inactive', then INSERT the config as 'active'. The two statements run on a plain pg.Client without BEGIN/COMMIT.

New `stash-forge install` downloads the EQL install SQL from GitHub releases/latest (unpinned) and executes it inside a transaction against the configured database; `--supabase` additionally grants anon/authenticated/service_role ALL on eql_v2 tables, routines and sequences and alters default privileges for role postgres.
New `stash-forge install --drizzle` shells out to `npx drizzle-kit generate --custom`, then overwrites the newest matching migration file with the downloaded latest EQL SQL.
@cipherstash/stack EncryptionClient gains a public getEncryptConfig() returning the validated internal encrypt config (additive; changeset marks stack minor).

New public npm package @cipherstash/stack-forge (ESM+CJS library entry, ESM bin `stash-forge`, engines node>=22) with a minor changeset; changeset config enables the experimental onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange option repo-wide.

stash-forge evaluates the user's stash.config.ts and encryption client file at runtime via jiti, and loads .env via dotenv at CLI start; the encryption client file is executed (initialising a real EncryptionClient) just to read its config.

failure_scenarios.title: push leaves the database with no active EQL configuration when the INSERT is rejected
failure_scenarios.trigger: Running `stash-forge push` with any schema that uses .dataType('number'|'bigint') or .searchableJson() (cast_as 'number', 'bigint' or 'json'), or any other INSERT failure (constraint, connection drop, missing table).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: push.ts runs `UPDATE eql_v2_configuration SET state = 'inactive'` and then `INSERT ... ('active', $1)` as separate autocommitted queries (push.ts:33-41, no BEGIN). The inserted data is the client's encrypt config, whose cast_as values come straight from the schema builder ('number', 'bigint', 'json'; schema/index.ts:27, 341). The EQL check constraint (bundled 2.1.8, cipherstash-encrypt-2-1-8.sql:3598-3650) only accepts {text, int, small_int, big_int, real, double, boolean, date, jsonb} and RAISEs otherwise. The UPDATE has already committed when the INSERT fails.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Previously active configuration is deactivated and no replacement is active. Anything that reads the active EQL config (EQL migration functions; Proxy-style consumers) loses its column configuration; depending on the consumer this breaks encrypted queries or stops encryption being applied to configured columns. The CLI exits 1 with the constraint error but does not restore state; manual SQL is needed to reactivate the old row.
missing_verification: An integration test pushing a schema with number/bigint/json columns into a database with EQL installed
A test that a failed INSERT leaves the previous active configuration intact
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Wrap UPDATE+INSERT in a single transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK); map client cast_as values to EQL's vocabulary (or reuse the mapping the client already uses for EQL) before inserting; validate against the constraint in --dry-run.

failure_scenarios.title: push silently discards pending/encrypting EQL configurations and overrides EQL's config lifecycle
failure_scenarios.trigger: `stash-forge push` against a database where an EQL encryption migration is in progress (a 'pending' or 'encrypting' row exists), or where the active config was managed by EQL functions/another tool.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The UPDATE has no WHERE clause (push.ts:33-35), so it moves 'pending' and 'encrypting' rows to 'inactive' as well as 'active'. EQL's own functions manage state transitions pending -> encrypting -> active (cipherstash-encrypt-2-1-8.sql:3368-3394). The pushed config fully replaces the active one with whatever the first EncryptionClient export in the client file contains (config/index.ts:170-186), with no diff or confirmation.
failure_scenarios.consequence: An in-flight encryption migration is abandoned without notice; columns configured outside this client file (other services sharing the database) drop out of the active configuration.
missing_verification: Test of push against a database with pending/encrypting rows
Review of intended interaction with EQL config lifecycle functions
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Restrict the UPDATE to state = 'active' (or refuse when pending/encrypting rows exist), use EQL's configuration functions where possible, and show a diff of the current vs new config before writing.

failure_scenarios.title: install applies an unpinned 'latest' EQL bundle that may not match the installed client library
failure_scenarios.trigger: A new EQL release is published on GitHub that is incompatible with the @cipherstash/stack version in the user's project, or the release asset changes/is unavailable.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Both the installer and the drizzle path fetch releases/latest/download/cipherstash-encrypt*.sql (installer/index.ts:4-6, install.ts:244) and execute or persist it with no version pin, checksum or compatibility check against the client. The profile notes client/SQL pairing as a contract.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Search terms produced by the client may not match the installed SQL functions, breaking encrypted queries; the same stash-forge version installs different SQL on different days, and generated Drizzle migrations are not reproducible across environments.

existing_verification.description: installer.test.ts asserts fetch is called with a URL and SQL runs inside BEGIN, with fetch and pg mocked

missing_verification: Compatibility check between installed EQL version and client version
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Pin the EQL release to a version tied to the stack-forge/stack release (or bundle the SQL in the package), and verify a checksum before executing.

failure_scenarios.title: --supabase grants broad privileges on the eql_v2 schema to anon and authenticated roles
failure_scenarios.mechanism: grantSupabasePermissions grants ALL on all tables, routines and sequences in eql_v2 to anon, authenticated and service_role and sets default privileges for role postgres (installer/index.ts:232-238).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Unauthenticated (anon) API clients gain write/execute rights on any present or future eql_v2 objects. What is exposed depends on the objects in the installed bundle, which was not enumerated; the configuration table itself is in public and is not covered by these grants.
missing_verification: Review of which eql_v2 objects anon actually needs (likely EXECUTE/USAGE only)
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Grant USAGE and EXECUTE only, and limit anon where possible; document the grants.
